```{r read_tables}

# study's, unedited.
source(file.path("..", "2026-11-15_gabitto", "helpers_claude.R"))
csv_dir <- "csv"
# A trial knit on small fits reads its tables from elsewhere.
if(Sys.getenv("GREEN_OUT_DIR") != ""){
  csv_dir <- file.path(Sys.getenv("GREEN_OUT_DIR"), "csv")
}
.read <- function(name){
  utils::read.csv(file.path(csv_dir, name), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
}
donor_df <- utils::read.csv(file.path("csv", "split_donors.csv"),
                            stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
balance_df <- utils::read.csv(file.path("csv", "split_balance.csv"),
                              stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
fit_df <- .read("fits.csv")
agreement_df <- .read("agreement.csv")
discovery_df <- .read("discovery.csv")
cross_df <- .read("cross_score.csv")
summary_df <- .read("summary.csv")
run_df <- .read("rule_runs.csv")
pair_df <- .read("gene_pairs.csv.gz")
calls_df <- .read("esvd_calls.csv")

split_vec <- c("split1", "split2")
method_vec <- unique(summary_df$method)
rule_vec <- c("stored", "null_rescaled", "deshrunk", "raw", "raw_null",
              "donor_wls", "gap_trend", "embed_prior", "state_adjusted")
# The methods that get a subsection of their own: the nine rules as the
# loops ran them, the two unfloored variants the beyond-score study
# recommended, and DESeq2.
section_vec <- c(rule_vec, "raw@esvd_nofloor", "donor_wls@esvd_nofloor",
                 "state_adjusted@esvd_nofloor", "deseq2")
stopifnot(all(section_vec %in% method_vec))

fmt <- function(x, digits = 2){formatC(x, digits = digits, format = "f")}
pct <- function(x, digits = 0){paste0(formatC(100 * x, digits = digits,
                                              format = "f"), "%")}
# One number of the summary table.
sm <- function(method, column, split){
  summary_df[summary_df$method == method & summary_df$split == split, column]
}
# The same number in the two splits, as "a and b".
both <- function(method, column, digits = 2, bool_pct = FALSE){
  value_vec <- sapply(split_vec, function(split){sm(method, column, split)})
  text_vec <- if(bool_pct) pct(value_vec) else fmt(value_vec, digits)
  paste0(text_vec[1], " and ", text_vec[2])
}
# One number of the agreement table.
ag <- function(method, gene_set, column, split){
  agreement_df[agreement_df$method == method & agreement_df$split == split &
                 agreement_df$gene_set == gene_set, column]
}
# The mean of a summary column over the two splits, for ranking.
avg <- function(column){
  value_vec <- tapply(summary_df[[column]], summary_df$method, mean)
  value_vec[method_vec]
}
# The method names with the best mean of a column.
best <- function(column, bool_low = TRUE, num = 1, among = method_vec){
  value_vec <- avg(column)[among]
  names(sort(value_vec, decreasing = !bool_low))[seq_len(num)]
}
# A methods x splits table of chosen summary columns.
wide_table <- function(column_vec, label_vec, digits = 2,
                       among = method_vec){
  out_df <- data.frame(method = among, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  for(idx in seq_along(column_vec)){
    for(split in split_vec){
      out_df[[paste0(label_vec[idx], ", ", split)]] <-
        sapply(among, function(method){sm(method, column_vec[idx], split)})
    }
  }
  out_df$method <- paste0("`", out_df$method, "`")
  knitr::kable(out_df, digits = digits, row.names = FALSE)
}
num_genes <- ag("stored", "all", "num_genes", "split1")
# One number of the table of eSVD-DE's calls.
cl <- function(group, column, split){

}
cl_both <- function(group, column, bool_pct = TRUE, digits = 2){

  text_vec <- if(bool_pct) pct(value_vec) else fmt(value_vec, digits)

}
ag_both <- function(method, gene_set, column, digits = 2){

}
# Method names as inline code, comma separated. A backtick cannot be typed

tick <- function(name_vec){
  paste0(intToUtf8(96), name_vec, intToUtf8(96), collapse = ", ")
}

gabitto_df <- utils::read.csv(file.path("..", "2026-11-15_gabitto", "csv",

# One correlation of the diagnosis table.
dg <- function(version, gene_set, split, cohort = "green"){

    diag_df$split == split & diag_df$cohort == cohort

}
dg_both <- function(version, gene_set, cohort = "green"){
  value_vec <- sapply(split_vec, function(split){
    dg(version, gene_set, split, cohort)
  })
  paste0(fmt(value_vec[1]), " and ", fmt(value_vec[2]))
}
# How many log donor means are outliers on the low side, per cohort.
outlying_df <- rbind(
  utils::read.csv(file.path("csv", "outlying_donors_green.csv"),
                  stringsAsFactors = FALSE),
  utils::read.csv(file.path("csv", "outlying_donors_gabitto.csv"),
                  stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
)
ol <- function(cohort, column){
  outlying_df[[column]][outlying_df$cohort == cohort]
}
state_vec <- grep("^state_adjusted", method_vec, value = TRUE)
keep_vec <- setdiff(method_vec, state_vec)

# Overview

This document is built from Kevin's note of 2026-11-16
(`2026-11-16_autoresearch-green-replicate.txt`), from the Gabitto
split-half study that it repeats
(`../2026-11-15_gabitto/2026-11-15_gabitto-split-half_claude.Rmd`), from
the two autoresearch loops on the reported log fold change and its
standard error and the study that followed them
(`2026-11-12_autoresearch_beyond-score_claude.Rmd`), and from Tati's
Writeup47 fit of the Green cohort (the design). The Green microglia are
split into two halves that share no donor, each half is fitted by eSVD-DE
on its own, and every rule is asked how well its logFC and SE from one
half agree with those from the other. The split is done twice. The
scripts, the statistics and the figures are those of the Gabitto study, so
that the two cohorts can be read side by side.

**The question.** On a second real cohort, with five times as many donors
as Gabitto and a third as many nuclei per donor, which rule's log2 fold
change and SE replicate best between two independent halves, and does the
recommendation from Gabitto hold?

What the document argues:

1. **The cohort has a different shape from Gabitto.** Each half has
   `r fit_df$num_donors[1]` donors (`r min(fit_df$num_control)` to
   `r max(fit_df$num_control)` controls) and about 41,000 nuclei, a median
   of `r round(stats::median(donor_df$num_cells))` per donor. The nuisance rate
   is at the cap for `r pct(min(fit_df$share_capped))` to
   `r pct(max(fit_df$share_capped))` of the genes (17% in the Gabitto
   halves), the package's test calls `r min(fit_df$num_esvd_deg)` to
   `r max(fit_df$num_esvd_deg)` genes per half at 5% FDR, and pseudobulk
   DESeq2 calls `r min(fit_df$num_deseq2_deg)` to
   `r max(fit_df$num_deseq2_deg)` (section 2.1).
2. **`state_adjusted` has the lowest replicate score again and almost no
   signal that replicates**, with
   `r fit_df$num_donors[1]` donors per half at rank 30: its halves
   correlate at `r both("state_adjusted", "all_pearson")` and a gene
   nominated by eSVD-DE's test keeps its sign in the other half
   `r both("state_adjusted", "esvd_sign_rep", bool_pct = TRUE)` of the
   time. A rank close to the number of donors is therefore not what
   removes the signal (section 4.1).
3. **Among the rules that keep a signal, `raw` on an unfloored library and
   pseudobulk DESeq2 score best, and `donor_wls@esvd_nofloor` is
   `r fmt(mean(c(sm("donor_wls@esvd_nofloor", "all_score", "split1") - sm("raw@esvd_nofloor", "all_score", "split1"), sm("donor_wls@esvd_nofloor", "all_score", "split2") - sm("raw@esvd_nofloor", "all_score", "split2"))))`
   nats behind `raw@esvd_nofloor`** (`raw@esvd_nofloor`
   `r both("raw@esvd_nofloor", "all_score")`, `deseq2`
   `r both("deseq2", "all_score")`, `donor_wls@esvd_nofloor`
   `r both("donor_wls@esvd_nofloor", "all_score")`, `stored`
   `r both("stored", "all_score")`). On Gabitto `donor_wls@esvd_nofloor`
   was first (section 4.2).
4. **The posterior's floor on the fitted library costs far more here than
   on Gabitto**:
   `r fmt(sm("donor_wls", "all_score", "split1") - sm("donor_wls@esvd_nofloor", "all_score", "split1"))`
   and
   `r fmt(sm("donor_wls", "all_score", "split2") - sm("donor_wls@esvd_nofloor", "all_score", "split2"))`
   nats for `donor_wls` and
   `r fmt(sm("raw", "all_score", "split1") - sm("raw@esvd_nofloor", "all_score", "split1"))`
   and
   `r fmt(sm("raw", "all_score", "split2") - sm("raw@esvd_nofloor", "all_score", "split2"))`
   for `raw` (section 4.2).
5. **`donor_wls` trails because a few donors lie far from the others on
   the log scale.** For the genes with under 80% zeros its halves
   correlate at `r ag_both("donor_wls@total", "zeros_below_80", "pearson")`
   with the summed-count library, against
   `r ag_both("raw@total", "zeros_below_80", "pearson")` for `raw` with the
   same library. Winsorizing each gene's log donor means brings
   `donor_wls` to `r dg_both("as the rule, winsorized", "zeros_below_80")`,
   and without the donor-level covariates to
   `r dg_both("no covariates, winsorized", "zeros_below_80")`. The same
   change does nothing on Gabitto (section 4.6).
6. **The SEs of `raw@esvd_nofloor`, `donor_wls@esvd_nofloor` and DESeq2
   are within 8% of the disagreement between the halves**, and the
   `stored` SE is twice too large (`z_rms`
   `r both("stored", "all_z_rms")`; section 4.4).
7. **A gene that eSVD-DE's test calls in one half keeps its sign in the
   other half `r cl_both("all calls", "sign_rep")` of the time.** The two
   flags that separated the calls on Gabitto (a nuisance rate at the cap,
   no support from `donor_wls`) do not separate them here (section 4.5).
8. **The recommendation**: on this cohort the pair to report is
   `raw@esvd_nofloor`; `donor_wls@esvd_nofloor` is close and needs a
   guard against outlying donors before it is used on a cohort of this
   shape. The simulated bank needs donors that are outliers on the log
   scale, many donors of few cells, and a capped share near 40%
   (section 5).

*How to read.* The blue box says how the cohort was split; green boxes
close each results subsection with what it changes; the orange box in
section 5 is the procedure. A reader of the boxes alone has the argument.

| Stage | What it does | Section |
|---|---|---|
| Definitions | the cohort, the two splits, the four fits, the rules, the statistics | 2 |
| Each rule | the two halves against each other, one subsection per rule | 3 |
| Side by side | the score, the correlation, the SE, the sign of the nominated genes, the diagnosis of `donor_wls`, Green beside Gabitto | 4 |
| Recommendation | the rule to report from and what the bank should add | 5 |

# Definitions

## The cohort and the two splits

The data are the microglia of the ROSMAP cohort of Green et al. (2024) as
cleaned for the Was2CoDE analysis
(`Writeup43_green_cleaned_only-counts.RData`):
`r format(sum(donor_df$num_cells), big.mark = ",")` nuclei of
`r nrow(donor_df)` donors and 5,256 genes, the same genes as the Gabitto
study. A donor is a case when `AD_path_cerad` is `TRUE`
(`r sum(donor_df$AD_path_cerad)` donors) and a control otherwise
(`r sum(!donor_df$AD_path_cerad)` donors), the definition of Tati's
Writeup47 fit of the whole cohort. A donor has a median of
`r round(stats::median(donor_df$num_cells))` nuclei, against about 500 in
Gabitto.

::: {.generator}
The `r nrow(donor_df)` donors fall into eight strata of CERAD arm, sex and
APOE4 status, as in the Gabitto study. Within each stratum the donors are permuted and dealt
alternately to two halves, and the half that receives the first donor
alternates over the strata with an odd count so that the leftover donors
do not all land in one half. A donor is therefore in exactly one half of a
split. The procedure is run twice with different seeds (`split1`, seed 10;
`split2`, seed 20), and
`r sum(donor_df$split1 == donor_df$split2)` of the `r nrow(donor_df)`
donors keep their half label between the two splits. Each of the four
halves is then fitted on its own with `eSVD2::eSVD_helper()` of
version 1.2.0 at the settings of Writeup47: `k = 30`, covariates `msex`,
`APOEe4_status`, `pmi` and `age_death`, every other argument at its
default.
:::

```{r tab_balance}
knitr::kable(balance_df, row.names = FALSE,
             caption = "Table 1. The donors of each half, by arm. PMI and age at death were not stratified on.")
```

```{r tab_fits}
show_df <- fit_df[, c("fit", "num_case", "num_control", "num_cells",
                      "num_genes", "fit_minutes", "null_mean", "null_sd",
                      "share_capped", "num_esvd_deg", "num_deseq2_deg")]
knitr::kable(show_df, digits = 2, row.names = FALSE,
             caption = "Table 2. The four fits. `null_mean` and `null_sd` are the empirical null of the package's test; `share_capped` is the share of genes whose nuisance rate sits at the cap; the last two columns count the genes called at 5% FDR by the package's test and by pseudobulk DESeq2.")
```

## The rules

Every rule is the file the loops left, unedited, applied as in the
beyond-score study (`2026-11-12_autoresearch_beyond-score_claude.Rmd`,
section 2.2) and in the Gabitto study.

| Name in the tables | Rule | Reads of the fit |
|---|---|---|
| `stored` | what 1.2.0 reports: log ratio of the arms' mean posterior, SE from the posterior's mixture variances | posterior |
| `null_rescaled` | `stored`, the logFC shifted by the empirical null's mean and the SE multiplied by its SD | posterior, empirical null |
| `deshrunk` | `stored`'s logFC; between-donor SE of the posterior donor means divided by the shrinkage weight | posterior, library, nuisance rate |
| `raw` | ratio of the arms' means of donor means of $A/\ell$, delta-method SE between donors | library |
| `raw_null` | `raw` with the empirical null's shift and rescaling | library |
| `donor_wls` | weighted regression of $\log\{(y_{dg} + 1/2)/L_{dg}\}$ on the arm and the donor-level covariates, residual variance moderated across genes, logFC shifted by the null's mean | library |
| `gap_trend` | as `donor_wls` with voom-style weights and a variance trend in a covariate that contains the between-arm gap | library |
| `embed_prior` | `donor_wls` with the embedding's predicted donor variance in the moderation prior | library, embedding |
| `state_adjusted` | `donor_wls` on summaries with the embedding's donor offset removed; the arm coefficients' component along the loadings subtracted | library, embedding |
| `deseq2` | DESeq2 on donor pseudobulk; design: sex, APOE4 status, PMI, age at death and the arm | nothing |

Here $y_{dg}$ is the donor's summed count and $L_{dg}$ its summed library.
A suffix names the library a library-reading rule was handed in place of
the fitted one: `@esvd_nofloor` (the fitted library before the posterior's
floor at 0.1), `@esvd_depth` (the fitted intercept and depth alone),
`@total` (the cell's summed counts), `@sf` and `@tmm` (summed counts
rescaled to DESeq2's size factors or edgeR's TMM factors of the donor
pseudobulk). `raw` is also run with `@esvd_nofloor` and `@total`, so
that it and `donor_wls` can be compared on one library; the Gabitto study
was rerun with the same two variants. Every covariate of this design is
constant within a donor, so the `_cov` variants of the beyond-score study
coincide with the plain ones.

## What is compared between the two halves

For one rule and one split, gene $g$ has the pair
$(\widehat{\beta}_{g1}, s_{g1})$ from half 1 and
$(\widehat{\beta}_{g2}, s_{g2})$ from half 2, on the $\log_2$ scale. The
two halves share no donor, so the two estimates are independent given the
population's effect.

**The replicate score.** The autoresearch score is the Gaussian negative
log-likelihood of the true effect under $N(\widehat{\beta}_g, s_g^2)$. A
real cohort has no known truth, and the other half takes its place: if
both halves estimate one effect and both SEs are honest, the difference
$\widehat{\beta}_{g1} - \widehat{\beta}_{g2}$ is
$N(0, s_{g1}^2 + s_{g2}^2)$, and the score is

$$
\text{score} = \frac{1}{p}\sum_{g=1}^{p}
\left[\tfrac{1}{2}\log\{2\pi (s_{g1}^2 + s_{g2}^2)\} +
\frac{(\widehat{\beta}_{g1} - \widehat{\beta}_{g2})^2}{2 (s_{g1}^2 + s_{g2}^2)}\right],
$$

in nats per gene, lower being better. It rewards estimates that agree and
SEs that match the size of the disagreement. The companion calibration
number is the root mean square of
$(\widehat{\beta}_{g1} - \widehat{\beta}_{g2}) / \sqrt{s_{g1}^2 + s_{g2}^2}$
(`z_rms`), which is 1 when the SEs explain the disagreement and above 1
when they are too small. The replicate score differs from the autoresearch
score in one respect that matters for reading it: a bias that the two
halves share (a depth artifact, shrinkage toward a common value) cancels
in the difference, so the replicate score cannot see it.

**The score against a common target.** To give every rule the same
target, each rule's pair from one half is also scored against the *other*
half's pseudobulk DESeq2 estimate, the difference having variance
$s_{g}^2$ plus DESeq2's squared SE, averaged over the two directions
(`score_cross`). A rule cannot lower this number through a bias its own
two halves share, and the comparison favours DESeq2's estimand (the
marginal effect on summed counts).

**Nominated genes.** A gene is nominated when it is called at 5% FDR in at
least one half, under three definitions: by eSVD-DE's own test (the
package's `fdr_vec`; the same genes for every rule), by pseudobulk DESeq2
(`padj`; the same genes for every rule), and by the rule's own Wald test,
$z = \widehat{\beta}_g / s_g$ against the standard normal with BH over the
half's genes (a different gene set per rule, whose size is reported).

**Statistics on the nominated genes.** The Pearson correlation of
$\widehat{\beta}_{g1}$ and $\widehat{\beta}_{g2}$ over the nominated
genes; the share of discoveries whose logFC has the same sign in the
other half (`sign_rep`, each discovery counted from its discovering half);
and the replication slope (`slope_rep`), the least-squares line through
the origin of the replication half's logFC on the discovering half's, the
convention of Writeup49. A slope of 1 means the discovered effects
reappear at full size, and the winner's curse puts it below 1.

# Each rule between the two halves

Each subsection shows one rule. The upper figure has every gene, coloured
by the half whose Wald test of the rule's own pair nominates it; the lower
figure has only the genes that eSVD-DE's test nominates in at least one
half, the same genes in every subsection. The dashed line is the diagonal,
and a gene beyond the axes is drawn on the edge.

```{r per_method, results='asis', fig.width=8, fig.height=4.8}
.panel_labels <- function(method, gene_set, nomination){
  do.call(rbind, lapply(split_vec, function(split){
    discovery_row <- discovery_df[discovery_df$split == split &
                                    discovery_df$method == method &
                                    discovery_df$nomination == nomination, ]
    data.frame(split = split,
               label = paste0(ag(method, gene_set, "num_genes", split),
                              " nominated genes\n",
                              "r = ", fmt(ag(method, gene_set, "pearson",
                                             split)),
                              ", same sign in the other half ",
                              pct(discovery_row$sign_rep), "\n",
                              "replication slope ",
                              fmt(discovery_row$slope_rep)),
               stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  }))
}
.method_table <- function(method){
  out_df <- data.frame(
    split = split_vec,
    score = sapply(split_vec, function(s){sm(method, "all_score", s)}),
    z_rms = sapply(split_vec, function(s){sm(method, "all_z_rms", s)}),
    r_all = sapply(split_vec, function(s){sm(method, "all_pearson", s)}),
    score_cross = sapply(split_vec, function(s){sm(method, "score_cross", s)}),
    own_genes = sapply(split_vec, function(s){sm(method, "own_num_genes", s)}),
    own_both = sapply(split_vec, function(s){sm(method, "own_num_both", s)}),
    own_r = sapply(split_vec, function(s){sm(method, "own_pearson", s)}),
    own_sign = sapply(split_vec, function(s){sm(method, "own_sign_rep", s)}),
    own_slope = sapply(split_vec, function(s){sm(method, "own_slope_rep", s)}),
    esvd_r = sapply(split_vec, function(s){sm(method, "esvd_pearson", s)}),
    esvd_sign = sapply(split_vec, function(s){sm(method, "esvd_sign_rep", s)}),
    esvd_slope = sapply(split_vec, function(s){sm(method, "esvd_slope_rep", s)}),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
  knitr::kable(out_df, digits = 2, row.names = FALSE)
}
for(method in section_vec){
  cat("\n\n## `", method, "`\n\n", sep = "")
  sub_df <- pair_df[pair_df$method == method, ]
  cat("Over all ", num_genes, " genes the replicate score of `", method,
      "` is ", both(method, "all_score"), " nats per gene in the two splits",
      " with `z_rms` ", both(method, "all_z_rms"),
      ", and the two halves' logFC correlate at ",
      both(method, "all_pearson"), ". Its own Wald test nominates ",
      sm(method, "own_num_genes", "split1"), " and ",
      sm(method, "own_num_genes", "split2"),
      " genes in at least one half, of which ",
      sm(method, "own_num_both", "split1"), " and ",
      sm(method, "own_num_both", "split2"), " in both halves.\n\n", sep = "")
  sub_df$nomination <- .nomination_factor(sub_df$own1, sub_df$own2)
  plot1 <- .plot_replication(
    plot_df = sub_df,
    label_df = .panel_labels(method, "nominated_own", "own"),
    title = paste0(method, ": all genes, coloured by the rule's own Wald ",
                   "test (BH 5%)"),
    bool_only_nominated = FALSE
  )
  plot(plot1)
  cat("\n\n")
  sub_df$nomination <- .nomination_factor(sub_df$esvd1, sub_df$esvd2)
  plot1 <- .plot_replication(
    plot_df = sub_df,
    label_df = .panel_labels(method, "nominated_esvd", "esvd"),
    title = paste0(method, ": genes nominated by eSVD-DE's test (FDR 5%) in ",
                   "at least one half"),
    bool_only_nominated = TRUE
  )
  plot(plot1)
  cat("\n\n")
  print(.method_table(method))
  cat("\n\n")
}
```

In each table, `score`, `z_rms` and `r_all` are over all genes; the
`own_` columns are over the genes the rule's own test nominates
(`own_genes` in at least one half, `own_both` in both); the `esvd_`
columns are over the genes eSVD-DE's test nominates.

# All rules side by side

```{r tab_summary}
wide_table(c("all_score", "score_cross", "all_z_rms", "all_pearson",
             "esvd_pearson", "esvd_sign_rep"),
           c("score", "score_cross", "z_rms", "corr_all", "corr_nominated",
             "sign_rep"))
```

Table 3. Every method in the two splits. `score`, `z_rms` and `corr_all` are
over all `r num_genes` genes; `corr_nominated` and `sign_rep` are over the
genes eSVD-DE's test nominates in at least one half
(`r sm("stored", "esvd_num_genes", "split1")` and
`r sm("stored", "esvd_num_genes", "split2")` genes).

## `state_adjusted` has the lowest replicate score and almost no signal, with 214 donors per half

```{r fig_score, fig.width=7, fig.height=5.6, fig.cap="Figure 1. The replicate score of every method over all genes, one point per split."}
plot1 <- .plot_summary(summary_df, "all_score",
                       "Replicate score over all genes (nats per gene, lower is better)",
                       method_vec)
plot(plot1)
```

The three `state_adjusted` variants score
`r fmt(min(avg("all_score")[state_vec]))` to
`r fmt(max(avg("all_score")[state_vec]))` nats per gene on average over
the two splits, and the best of the other methods scores
`r fmt(min(avg("all_score")[keep_vec]))`. The same rule's two halves
correlate at `r both("state_adjusted", "all_pearson")` over all genes and
at `r both("state_adjusted", "esvd_pearson")` over the genes eSVD-DE's
test nominates, where every rule that keeps a signal is above
`r fmt(min(summary_df$esvd_pearson[summary_df$method %in% keep_vec]))`.
The sign of a nominated gene holds in the other half
`r both("state_adjusted", "esvd_sign_rep", bool_pct = TRUE)` of the time.
The SD of its logFC across genes is
`r ag_both("state_adjusted", "all", "sd_lfc")` against
`r ag_both("donor_wls@esvd_nofloor", "all", "sd_lfc")` for
`donor_wls@esvd_nofloor`, and its `z_rms` is
`r both("state_adjusted", "all_z_rms")`: small logFC with a matching SE,
as on Gabitto. Against the other half's DESeq2 its logFC correlate at
`r both("state_adjusted", "pearson_cross")`, where `donor_wls@esvd_nofloor`
has `r both("donor_wls@esvd_nofloor", "pearson_cross")`.

The Gabitto report attributed the loss to a fitted rank of 30 with 40
donors per half, an embedding wide enough to carry most donor-level
contrasts. The Green halves have `r fit_df$num_donors[1]` donors at the
same rank, and the correlation between the halves is still at most
`r fmt(max(summary_df$all_pearson[summary_df$method %in% state_vec]))`.
The rank relative to the number of donors is therefore not a sufficient
explanation. What the two cohorts share is a rank of 30 on real microglia,
where the leading loadings may themselves be aligned with the
case-control contrast, the second condition the loop's report had flagged
as untested.

::: {.takeaway}
`state_adjusted` fails on Green in the way it failed on Gabitto: the
lowest replicate score, logFC with about 60% of the spread of the other
rules, and a correlation between halves near 0.1. With 214 donors per
half the fitted rank is far below the donor count, so the failure is not
specific to small cohorts. The rule is left out of the rankings below.
:::

## Among the rules that keep a signal, `raw` on an unfloored library and DESeq2 score best

```{r fig_cross, fig.width=7, fig.height=5.6, fig.cap="Figure 2. Each method's pair from one half scored against the other half's pseudobulk DESeq2 estimate, averaged over the two directions; one point per split."}
plot1 <- .plot_summary(summary_df, "score_cross",
                       "Score against the other half's DESeq2 (nats per gene, lower is better)",
                       method_vec)
plot(plot1)
```

Without `state_adjusted`, the lowest mean replicate score belongs to
`r tick(best("all_score", num = 4, among = keep_vec))`, in that order, and
the lowest mean score against the other half's DESeq2 to
`r tick(best("score_cross", num = 4, among = keep_vec))`. `gap_trend` is
the rule the first loop withdrew because its SE follows the estimated
logFC, and it stays withdrawn. Of the rest, `raw@total` scores
`r both("raw@total", "all_score")`, `raw@esvd_nofloor`
`r both("raw@esvd_nofloor", "all_score")`, `deseq2`
`r both("deseq2", "all_score")`, `donor_wls@esvd_nofloor`
`r both("donor_wls@esvd_nofloor", "all_score")`, `null_rescaled`
`r both("null_rescaled", "all_score")` and `stored`
`r both("stored", "all_score")`. The four leaders are within 0.09 nats of
each other, and `stored` is 0.3 to 0.4 behind them.

**The floor on the library.** The rules as the loops ran them read the
fitted library floored at 0.1, and on this cohort that library is costly:
`donor_wls` scores `r both("donor_wls", "all_score")` with it and
`r both("donor_wls@esvd_nofloor", "all_score")` without, and `raw`
`r both("raw", "all_score")` against
`r both("raw@esvd_nofloor", "all_score")`. With the floor `donor_wls`
has a `z_rms` of `r both("donor_wls", "all_z_rms")` and its halves
correlate at `r both("donor_wls", "all_pearson")` over all genes. The
Gabitto halves lost 0.05 and 0.01 nats to the floor. A Green donor has a
third of the nuclei of a Gabitto donor, and
`r pct(mean(fit_df$share_capped))` of the genes are at the nuisance cap.

**The library without the floor.** For `raw` the summed counts and the
unfloored fitted library are equivalent (`r both("raw@total", "all_score")`
against `r both("raw@esvd_nofloor", "all_score")`). For `donor_wls` the
fitted library is better by
`r fmt(sm("donor_wls@total", "all_score", "split1") - sm("donor_wls@esvd_nofloor", "all_score", "split1"))`
and
`r fmt(sm("donor_wls@total", "all_score", "split2") - sm("donor_wls@esvd_nofloor", "all_score", "split2"))`
nats, and `@esvd_depth` equals `@esvd_nofloor` to 0.001, so the gain comes
from the gene-specific depth coefficient and not from the covariate
columns. Section 4.6 shows that the summed-count version is the one most
exposed to outlying donors.

```{r tab_sparsity}
strata_method_vec <- c("stored", "null_rescaled", "raw", "raw@esvd_nofloor",
                       "raw@total", "donor_wls", "donor_wls@esvd_nofloor",
                       "donor_wls@total", "deseq2")
set_vec <- c(zeros_below_80 = "under 80% zeros",
             zeros_80_to_95 = "80 to 95% zeros",
             zeros_above_95 = "over 95% zeros",
             rate_estimated = "rate estimated", rate_capped = "rate at the cap")
out_df <- data.frame(method = paste0("`", strata_method_vec, "`"),
                     stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
for(gene_set in names(set_vec)){
  out_df[[set_vec[[gene_set]]]] <- sapply(strata_method_vec, function(method){
    mean(sapply(split_vec, function(split){
      ag(method, gene_set, "score", split)
    }))
  })
}
count_vec <- sapply(names(set_vec), function(gene_set){
  ag("stored", gene_set, "num_genes", "split1")
})
knitr::kable(out_df, digits = 2, row.names = FALSE,
             caption = paste0("Table 4. The replicate score by gene stratum, mean of the two splits. Genes per stratum in split 1: ", paste0(set_vec, " ", count_vec, collapse = "; "), "."))
```

::: {.takeaway}
On Green the rules that lead are `raw` with an unfloored library and
pseudobulk DESeq2, with `donor_wls@esvd_nofloor` 0.03 to 0.07 nats
behind, where on Gabitto `donor_wls@esvd_nofloor` led by up to 0.06. What
holds on both cohorts is that `stored` is far behind and that the floor
on the library should go; on Green the floor costs `donor_wls` 0.25 to
0.40 nats.
:::

## Correlation over the nominated genes

```{r fig_nominated, fig.width=7, fig.height=5.6, fig.cap="Figure 3. Correlation of the two halves' logFC over the genes that eSVD-DE's test nominates in at least one half (the same genes for every method); one point per split."}
plot1 <- .plot_summary(summary_df, "esvd_pearson",
                       "Correlation between the halves, genes nominated by eSVD-DE's test",
                       method_vec)
plot(plot1)
```

Over the genes eSVD-DE's test nominates, the highest mean correlation
between the halves belongs to
`r tick(best("esvd_pearson", bool_low = FALSE, num = 4, among = keep_vec))`.
`donor_wls@esvd_nofloor` has `r both("donor_wls@esvd_nofloor", "esvd_pearson")`,
`raw@esvd_nofloor` `r both("raw@esvd_nofloor", "esvd_pearson")`, `raw`
`r both("raw", "esvd_pearson")`, `stored` `r both("stored", "esvd_pearson")`
and `deseq2` `r both("deseq2", "esvd_pearson")`. Over the
`r sm("stored", "deseq2_num_genes", "split1")` and
`r sm("stored", "deseq2_num_genes", "split2")` genes that DESeq2
nominates, `donor_wls@esvd_nofloor` has
`r both("donor_wls@esvd_nofloor", "deseq2_pearson")`, `raw@esvd_nofloor`
`r both("raw@esvd_nofloor", "deseq2_pearson")` and `deseq2`
`r both("deseq2", "deseq2_pearson")`. On the nominated genes, which are
the genes with the larger effects, `donor_wls@esvd_nofloor` is at least
as good as `raw@esvd_nofloor` in both splits; over all genes the order is
the reverse (`r both("donor_wls@esvd_nofloor", "all_pearson")` against
`r both("raw@esvd_nofloor", "all_pearson")`).

```{r tab_own}
wide_table(c("own_num_half1", "own_num_half2", "own_num_both", "own_sign_rep",
             "own_slope_rep"),
           c("half 1", "half 2", "both", "sign_rep", "slope_rep"),
           among = c("null_rescaled", "raw", "raw@esvd_nofloor", "raw@total",
                     "raw_null@esvd_nofloor", "donor_wls",
                     "donor_wls@esvd_nofloor", "donor_wls@total", "deseq2"))
```

Table 5. Each rule's own nominations (BH 5% on its Wald test): genes
nominated per half and in both, the share of discoveries with the same
sign in the other half, and the replication slope.

With `r min(fit_df$num_control)` controls or more per half the calibrated
rules nominate genes of their own, which they could not on Gabitto.
`donor_wls@esvd_nofloor` nominates
`r sm("donor_wls@esvd_nofloor", "own_num_genes", "split1")` and
`r sm("donor_wls@esvd_nofloor", "own_num_genes", "split2")` genes in at
least one half and its discoveries keep their sign
`r both("donor_wls@esvd_nofloor", "own_sign_rep", bool_pct = TRUE)` of
the time; `raw@esvd_nofloor` nominates
`r sm("raw@esvd_nofloor", "own_num_genes", "split1")` and
`r sm("raw@esvd_nofloor", "own_num_genes", "split2")` with
`r both("raw@esvd_nofloor", "own_sign_rep", bool_pct = TRUE)`, and
`deseq2` `r sm("deseq2", "own_num_genes", "split1")` and
`r sm("deseq2", "own_num_genes", "split2")` with
`r both("deseq2", "own_sign_rep", bool_pct = TRUE)`. The package's test
nominates `r sm("stored", "esvd_num_genes", "split1")` and
`r sm("stored", "esvd_num_genes", "split2")` genes with a sign agreement
of `r cl_both("all calls", "sign_rep")`. `null_rescaled` and the floored
`raw` and `donor_wls` nominate two to three times as many genes as the
unfloored rules at a lower sign agreement.

::: {.takeaway}
On the nominated genes `donor_wls@esvd_nofloor` replicates as well as or
better than `raw@esvd_nofloor`, and both do better than `stored` in at
least one split. The three calibrated tests (`raw@esvd_nofloor`,
`donor_wls@esvd_nofloor`, DESeq2) nominate 95 to 135 genes per split whose
sign holds in the other half about nine times in ten, against eight in
ten for the package's test.
:::

## The SE against the disagreement between the halves

```{r fig_zrms, fig.width=7, fig.height=5.6, fig.cap="Figure 4. Root mean square of the standardized difference between the halves; 1 (dashed) means the SEs explain the disagreement, below 1 that they are too large."}
plot1 <- .plot_summary(summary_df, "all_z_rms",
                       "RMS of (lfc1 - lfc2) / sqrt(se1^2 + se2^2)",
                       method_vec, reference = 1)
plot(plot1)
```

The `stored` SE gives a `z_rms` of `r both("stored", "all_z_rms")`, an SE
about twice the one that would explain the disagreement between the
halves (2.3 to 2.6 times on Gabitto). `null_rescaled` is at
`r both("null_rescaled", "all_z_rms")`: the empirical null's SD of
`r fmt(min(fit_df$null_sd))` to `r fmt(max(fit_df$null_sd))` repairs the
`stored` SE on this cohort over all genes, with
`r ag_both("null_rescaled", "zeros_below_80", "z_rms")` for the genes
under 80% zeros and `r ag_both("null_rescaled", "zeros_above_95", "z_rms")`
for those over 95%. `raw@esvd_nofloor` is at
`r both("raw@esvd_nofloor", "all_z_rms")`, `donor_wls@esvd_nofloor` at
`r both("donor_wls@esvd_nofloor", "all_z_rms")` and `deseq2` at
`r both("deseq2", "all_z_rms")`, all slightly too small. On Gabitto
`donor_wls@esvd_nofloor` was at 0.85 to 0.89, so its SE moved from about
15% too large with 40 donors to about 6% too small with 214. The floored `raw` and
`donor_wls` are at `r both("raw", "all_z_rms")` and
`r both("donor_wls", "all_z_rms")`.

::: {.takeaway}
The stored SE is twice too large on Green as well. The SEs of
`raw@esvd_nofloor`, `donor_wls@esvd_nofloor` and DESeq2 are 4 to 8% too
small against the disagreement between the halves, close enough that the
choice between the three rules does not rest on calibration.
:::

## Does a nominated gene keep its sign in the other half?

```{r fig_sign, fig.width=7, fig.height=5.6, fig.cap="Figure 5. Share of the genes called by eSVD-DE's test in one half whose logFC, under each method, has the same sign in the other half; one point per split."}
plot1 <- .plot_summary(summary_df, "esvd_sign_rep",
                       "Same sign in the other half, genes nominated by eSVD-DE's test",
                       method_vec, reference = 0.5)
plot(plot1)
```

```{r tab_calls}
show_df <- calls_df[, c("split", "group", "num_calls", "sign_rep",
                        "sign_rep_wls", "slope_rep", "median_abs_lfc")]
knitr::kable(show_df, digits = 2, row.names = FALSE,
             caption = "Table 6. The genes eSVD-DE's test calls at 5% FDR in one half, by group. `sign_rep` uses the `stored` logFC of the two halves and `sign_rep_wls` that of `donor_wls@esvd_nofloor`; `slope_rep` is the replication slope of the `stored` logFC; the `donor_wls` p-value is the nominal Wald p of `donor_wls@esvd_nofloor` in the discovering half.")
```

Of the genes eSVD-DE's test calls in one half,
`r cl_both("all calls", "sign_rep")` have a `stored` logFC of the same
sign in the other half (Table 6), which bounds the share of null genes
among the calls at
`r pct(2 * (1 - cl("all calls", "sign_rep", "split1")))` and
`r pct(2 * (1 - cl("all calls", "sign_rep", "split2")))` (a null gene
keeps its sign half the time). The Gabitto halves had 81% and 66%.

The two flags of the Gabitto report behave differently here. A call whose
gene has its nuisance rate at the cap keeps its `stored` sign
`r cl_both("rate at the cap", "sign_rep")` of the time against
`r cl_both("rate estimated", "sign_rep")` for the other calls, so the
capped calls replicate at least as well, as they did in the comparison
with Prater. A call that `donor_wls@esvd_nofloor` supports at nominal
$p < 0.05$ keeps its `stored` sign
`r cl_both("donor_wls p < 0.05", "sign_rep")` of the time against
`r cl_both("donor_wls p >= 0.05", "sign_rep")` for the unsupported calls,
a difference of a few points. The unsupported calls differ in another
respect: their replication slope is
`r cl_both("donor_wls p >= 0.05", "slope_rep", bool_pct = FALSE)` against
`r cl_both("donor_wls p < 0.05", "slope_rep", bool_pct = FALSE)`, and
under the `donor_wls@esvd_nofloor` logFC their sign holds
`r cl_both("donor_wls p >= 0.05", "sign_rep_wls")` of the time. For these
genes the posterior-based logFC and the donor-level logFC disagree, the
first keeps a small effect of stable sign in both halves, and the second
does not see it.

::: {.takeaway}
About eight to nine of ten eSVD-DE calls keep their sign in the other
half on Green. Neither the nuisance status nor the `donor_wls` p-value
separates the calls that keep their `stored` sign from those that do not,
so step 4 of the Gabitto procedure (treat a capped or unsupported call as
provisional) does not carry over as a rule. The unsupported calls are
genes on which the posterior-based and the donor-level estimates
disagree in size and sign.
:::

## Why `donor_wls` trails `raw` here: donors that are outliers on the log scale

`donor_wls` and `raw` were handed the same library in the `@total`
variants, and their halves agree very differently on the well-expressed
genes: `r ag_both("raw@total", "zeros_below_80", "pearson")` for `raw@total`
against `r ag_both("donor_wls@total", "zeros_below_80", "pearson")` for
`donor_wls@total` over the genes with under 80% zeros, and
`r ag_both("raw@total", "rate_capped", "pearson")` against
`r ag_both("donor_wls@total", "rate_capped", "pearson")` over the genes at
the cap. `donor_wls` reads the counts and the library only through their
sums per donor, so `05_diagnose-donor-wls_claude.R` reran it from the
donor pseudobulk with one step changed at a time; the unchanged version
reproduces the stored `donor_wls@total` exactly.

```{r tab_diagnosis}
version_vec <- c("as the rule", "no donor offset", "no weights",
                 "no covariates", "no covariates, no offset, no weights",
                 "as the rule, winsorized", "no covariates, winsorized",
                 "raw (donor sums)", "raw@total (stored)", "deseq2 (stored)")
diag_table <- function(cohort){
  out_df <- data.frame(version = version_vec, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  for(gene_set in c("all", "zeros_below_80", "rate_capped")){
    for(split in split_vec){
      out_df[[paste0(gene_set, ", ", split)]] <- sapply(version_vec, function(version){
        dg(version, gene_set, split, cohort)
      })
    }
  }
  out_df
}
knitr::kable(diag_table("green"), digits = 2, row.names = FALSE,
             caption = "Table 7. Green: correlation of the logFC between the halves for versions of `donor_wls` with the summed-count library, over all genes, the genes with under 80% zeros and the genes at the nuisance cap. `no covariates` leaves the intercept and the arm in the donor-level design; `winsorized` pulls each gene's log donor means to within 3 MADs of the gene's median before anything is fitted.")
knitr::kable(diag_table("gabitto"), digits = 2, row.names = FALSE,
             caption = "Table 8. The same on the Gabitto halves.")
```

Neither the donor offset nor the precision weights matters (Table 7). The
donor-level covariates cost agreement, from
`r dg_both("as the rule", "all")` with them to
`r dg_both("no covariates", "all")` without over all genes. The step that
matters most is the mean of logarithms itself: with no covariates, offset
or weights the rule is the difference between the arms of the mean log
donor mean, which correlates at
`r dg_both("no covariates, no offset, no weights", "zeros_below_80")`
between the halves over the genes with under 80% zeros, while the log
ratio of arithmetic means of the same donor values (`raw (donor sums)`)
correlates at `r dg_both("raw (donor sums)", "zeros_below_80")`.
Winsorizing each gene's log donor means at 3 MADs raises the first to
`r dg_both("no covariates, winsorized", "zeros_below_80")`, above `raw`,
and raises the rule with its covariates from
`r dg_both("as the rule", "zeros_below_80")` to
`r dg_both("as the rule, winsorized", "zeros_below_80")`. A few donors
whose log mean for a gene lies far from the others' therefore account for
the loss: a mean of logarithms gives a donor at a tenth of the typical
expression a weight that an arithmetic mean does not. On the Gabitto
halves, with about 500 nuclei per donor, the same winsorization changes
no correlation by more than 0.02 (Table 8), and there `donor_wls` agrees
between the halves as well as `raw` does over all genes.

**How many such donors.** Over the genes with under 80% zeros,
`r pct(ol("green", "share_below_3"), 1)` of the log donor means of the
Green cohort lie more than 3 MADs below the gene's median and
`r pct(ol("green", "share_below_5"), 1)` more than 5, where a Gaussian
has 0.1% beyond 3; on the Gabitto cohort the shares are
`r pct(ol("gabitto", "share_below_3"), 1)` and
`r pct(ol("gabitto", "share_below_5"), 2)`. A Green outlier is
`r fmt(-ol("green", "mean_deficit"), 1)` below the median on the
natural-log scale on average, about an eighth of the typical expression,
and a Gabitto one `r fmt(-ol("gabitto", "mean_deficit"), 1)`. The Green
outliers sit in a minority of donors:
`r pct(ol("green", "share_donors_outlying"))` of the donors have a tenth
or more of their genes below the threshold (the largest share is
`r pct(ol("green", "max_donor_share"))`; no Gabitto donor is above
`r pct(ol("gabitto", "max_donor_share"))`), and a donor's share
correlates at `r fmt(ol("green", "cor_with_log_depth"))` with its log
depth per nucleus, so they are the donors sequenced most shallowly.

The unfloored fitted library softens the problem without removing it
(`donor_wls@esvd_nofloor` has
`r ag_both("donor_wls@esvd_nofloor", "zeros_below_80", "pearson")` over
the genes with under 80% zeros, against
`r ag_both("raw@esvd_nofloor", "zeros_below_80", "pearson")` for
`raw@esvd_nofloor`).

::: {.takeaway}
`donor_wls` loses to `raw` on Green because it averages logarithms over
donors of whom about one in nine is far below the rest for a tenth or
more of its genes; `raw` averages on the natural scale and is not moved by a
donor with low expression. Winsorized log donor means agree between the
halves better than either rule. The donor-level covariates of
`donor_wls` cost agreement on this cohort and make little difference on
Gabitto.
:::

## Green beside Gabitto

```{r tab_cohorts}
compare_vec <- c("stored", "null_rescaled", "raw@esvd_nofloor", "raw@total",
                 "donor_wls", "donor_wls@esvd_nofloor", "donor_wls@total",
                 "state_adjusted", "deseq2")
column_vec <- c(all_score = "score", score_cross = "score_cross",
                all_z_rms = "z_rms", all_pearson = "corr_all",
                esvd_pearson = "corr_nominated", esvd_sign_rep = "sign_rep")
out_df <- data.frame(method = paste0("`", compare_vec, "`"),
                     stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
for(column in names(column_vec)){
  out_df[[paste0(column_vec[[column]], ", Gabitto")]] <-
    sapply(compare_vec, function(method){
      mean(gabitto_df[[column]][gabitto_df$method == method])
    })
  out_df[[paste0(column_vec[[column]], ", Green")]] <-
    sapply(compare_vec, function(method){
      mean(summary_df[[column]][summary_df$method == method])
    })
}
knitr::kable(out_df, digits = 2, row.names = FALSE,
             caption = "Table 9. The two cohorts side by side, each number the mean of the cohort's two splits. The scores are not comparable between cohorts (the SEs are smaller with more donors); the order of the rules within a cohort is.")
```

The two cohorts agree on four things: `stored` has the worst score of
the rules that keep a signal and an SE two to two and a half times too
large; `state_adjusted` wins the replicate score with no agreement
between its halves; removing the floor from the library helps every rule
that reads it; and the calibrated rules are within 0.08 nats of each
other and of DESeq2. They disagree on the order of `raw@esvd_nofloor`
and `donor_wls@esvd_nofloor`: `donor_wls@esvd_nofloor` leads on Gabitto
by `r fmt(mean(gabitto_df$all_score[gabitto_df$method == "raw@esvd_nofloor"]) - mean(gabitto_df$all_score[gabitto_df$method == "donor_wls@esvd_nofloor"]))`
nats on average and trails on Green by
`r fmt(mean(summary_df$all_score[summary_df$method == "donor_wls@esvd_nofloor"]) - mean(summary_df$all_score[summary_df$method == "raw@esvd_nofloor"]))`.

::: {.takeaway}
Between the two candidates for the reported pair the cohorts split:
`donor_wls@esvd_nofloor` on Gabitto (80 donors of about 500 nuclei),
`raw@esvd_nofloor` on Green (428 donors of about 190). The reason on
Green is identified (section 4.6) and is a property of the mean of
logarithms with many small donors.
:::

# Recommendation

**Which rule on this cohort.** By the replicate score and the score
against an independent DESeq2 estimate, `raw@esvd_nofloor` is the best
rule from eSVD-DE on Green that the loops did not withdraw, level with
`raw@total` and DESeq2, and its SE is 6% too small against the
disagreement between the halves. This is a consequence of the evidence
above. `donor_wls@esvd_nofloor`, the recommendation of the Gabitto
report, is 0.03 to 0.07 nats behind it, replicates as well on the
nominated genes, and loses on the well-expressed genes for the reason of
section 4.6.

**Which library.** Without the floor, in every case (a consequence,
measured at 0.13 to 0.40 nats on this cohort). Between the unfloored
fitted library and the summed counts, `raw` is indifferent and
`donor_wls` is better with the fitted library.

**Which rule not.** `state_adjusted` (a consequence, second cohort),
`stored` as the reported SE (a consequence, fourth time measured), and
any rule with the floored library on a cohort of this shape.

**How to read an eSVD-DE call.** The sign of a call holds in the other
half 79% and 88% of the time. The two flags of the Gabitto procedure do
not identify the calls that fail here, so no flag is recommended from
this cohort (a consequence).

::: {.recipe}
1. Fit the cohort with `eSVD2::eSVD_helper()` as now.
2. Rebuild the counts and the covariates of the fit and form the fitted
   library without the posterior's floor, the exponential of the fit's
   linear predictor over every covariate but the arm.
3. Report the log2 fold change and its SE from `raw@esvd_nofloor`.
4. Beside it, compute `donor_wls@esvd_nofloor` and the share of log
   donor means more than 3 MADs below the gene's median (2.3% here, 0.8%
   on Gabitto). Where the two logFC of a gene disagree in sign or by
   more than their SEs, the gene's log donor means should be inspected
   for outlying donors.
5. Check on a split of the cohort's donors, as here, that the reported
   rule's two halves correlate over the nominated genes and over the
   well-expressed genes.
6. Replacement: on a cohort with few donors of many cells each (the
   Gabitto shape), `donor_wls@esvd_nofloor` is the pair to report, as in
   the Gabitto report. The final choice between the two rules across
   cohort shapes is made in
   `2026-11-16_autoresearch_beyond-score_claude.Rmd`, which has the
   simulated evidence beside both cohorts.
:::

**What the autoresearch bank should add.** Three things on this cohort
were outside what the banks could show, beyond the four of the Gabitto
report.

1. *Donors that are outliers on the log scale.* Every bank draws donor
   effects from a Gaussian on the log scale, under which a mean of
   logarithms is the efficient summary. Examples in which a tenth of the
   donors lie far below the others for a share of their genes, at the
   rate and size measured here, separate `raw` from `donor_wls` in
   simulation.
2. *Many donors of few cells.* The banks stop at 40 donors. Examples
   with 200 donors of 50 to 200 cells have small per-donor counts for
   most genes, which is where the half count and the logarithm of
   `donor_wls` matter.
3. *A capped share near 40%.* The Gabitto halves have 17% of genes at
   the cap and the Green halves 43%, with the floor on the library
   costing several times as much.

The fourth bank, `lfcse-bank-4`, has these three beside the four of the
Gabitto report; it is described and scored in
`2026-11-16_autoresearch_beyond-score_claude.Rmd`. With outlying donors
drawn at Green's rate it reproduces the order found here (`donor_wls`
behind `raw` and DESeq2), and with Gaussian donors `donor_wls` is ahead
of `raw` at 200 donors as at 40, so the number of donors is not what
reverses the order.

# What we glossed over

- **Two splits of one cohort.** The two splits share all
  `r nrow(donor_df)` donors, and
  `r sum(donor_df$split1 == donor_df$split2)` donors have the same half
  label in both, so their agreement is not independent confirmation.
  Differences of under 0.03 nats or 0.05 in a correlation are within the
  variation between the splits.
- **Shared bias is invisible to a split.** A bias common to both halves
  cancels in the difference and raises the correlation. The simulated
  banks, which have a truth, are the evidence against such a bias, and
  the score against the other half's DESeq2 is a partial check.
- **Why the shallow donors are outlying was not examined.** Section 4.6
  shows that bounding each gene's log donor means restores the
  agreement and that the outlying values sit in the donors of low depth
  per nucleus; whether the cause is technical (ambient RNA, a batch) or
  a distinct microglial state was not studied. Winsorized log donor
  means are a diagnostic here and not a proposed rule.
- **Why the covariates cost agreement was not dissected.** APOE4 status
  differs between the arms (9 of 76 controls against 46 of 138 cases per
  half), so the arm coefficient loses precision to it; whether that
  accounts for the whole loss was not tested.
- **One fit used a fallback null.** In `split2_half2` `locfdr` did not
  converge and the package's test used its truncated maximum-likelihood
  estimator (null SD 0.44, within the range of the other three fits).
- **The rules' own tests use a normal reference**, which matters little
  with 208 residual degrees of freedom.
- **Each half has half the cohort's power**, so the counts of nominated
  genes describe cohorts of 214 donors.
- **Batch and study are not adjusted for**, as in Writeup47 (127 batches,
  two studies, ROS and MAP), and no split stratified on them, on PMI or
  on age at death (Table 1 shows the realized means).
- **The fits stopped after 9 to 11 iterations per phase** at the default
  tolerance and took 66 to 83 minutes each. Four fits at once need about
  50 GB during the nuisance step, more than the laptop's 32 GB, and two
  of them were paused until the other two had finished.
- **Why `state_adjusted` loses the signal is still not dissected**; the
  rank explanation of the Gabitto report is ruled out as sufficient.

# Files

All paths are relative to `additional_context/2026-11-16_green/` unless
they start with `OUT`, which is `out/2026-11-16_green/` beside the
repository clone (not in git).

| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| `paths_claude.R` | the data file, the output folder and the design shared by every step |
| `01_split-donors_claude.R` | the two stratified splits; writes `csv/split_donors.csv` (one row per donor), `csv/split_balance.csv` and `OUT/green_splits.RData` |
| `02_fit-esvd_claude.R <label>` | one eSVD-DE fit; writes `OUT/green_<label>_esvd.RData` (the diet `eSVD` object) |
| `03_apply-rules_claude.R <label>` | every rule, variant and DESeq2 on one fitted half; writes `OUT/green_<label>_rules.RData` (genes x methods matrices of logFC and SE) |
| `04_evaluate_claude.R` | the comparisons; writes `OUT/green_evaluation.RData`, `OUT/figures/*.png` and the tables below |
| `05_diagnose-donor-wls_claude.R <green\|gabitto>` | `donor_wls` with the summed-count library rerun from the donor pseudobulk, one step changed at a time; writes `csv/donor_wls_diagnosis_<cohort>.csv` (one row per split, version and gene set) and `csv/outlying_donors_<cohort>.csv` (one row: how many log donor means are outliers on the low side) |
| `../2026-11-15_gabitto/helpers_claude.R` | the replication statistics and the two figure functions, shared with the Gabitto study |
| `csv/fits.csv` | one row per fit |
| `csv/agreement.csv` | one row per split, method and gene set: score, `z_rms`, coverage, correlations, sign agreement |
| `csv/discovery.csv` | one row per split, method and nomination: discoveries per half, `sign_rep`, `slope_rep`, share replicated at nominal p < 0.05 |
| `csv/cross_score.csv` | one row per split and method: the score against the other half's DESeq2 |
| `csv/esvd_calls.csv` | one row per split and group of eSVD-DE's calls: number of calls, sign agreement, replication slope |
| `csv/summary.csv` | one row per split and method, the columns of the tables above side by side |
| `csv/rule_runs.csv` | one row per fit and method: error message (empty when the rule ran) and seconds |
| `csv/gene_pairs.csv.gz` | one row per split, method and gene: the two halves' logFC and SE and the nominations; the figures of section 3 are drawn from it |
| `run_after-fits_claude.sh` | waits for the four fits, then runs step 3 on each and step 4 |
| `output/` | the logs of the four fits and of steps 3 and 4 |
